, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT Heard learned counsel appearing for the claimant- appellant and the learned counsel appearing for the insurer and the learned counsel for respondent No.4.
2. The petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation on account of injuries suffered by the claimant is allowed in part awarding compensation of Rs.3,89,000/-.
The tribunal also awarded 9% interest on the compensation.
However, the liability is fixed on respondent No.4 who, according to the Tribunal, was the owner of the vehicle at the time of the accident.
3. The claimant is before this Court challenging the judgment and award and seeks to impose the liability on the insurer, the owner of the vehicle as on the date of the accident.
The claimant is also seeking enhancement of the compensation.

sentences.text: 4. The learned counsel for the appellant would submit that as on the date of the accident, the vehicle stood in the name of the 2nd respondent, who had financed its customer and the customer, who has purchased the vehicle after availing loan from 2nd respondent could not repay the amount as such the vehicle was seized and after the vehicle was seized the vehicle was transferred in the name of the 2nd respondent-financier.
The records would reveal that as on the date of the accident, the vehicle stood in the name of the 2nd respondent.
The learned counsel for the appellant would submit that the appellant has filed an application under Order XLI Rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to produce the additional documents.
This Court has perused the said additional document, and it is forthcoming that as on the date of the accident, the vehicle stood in the name of the 2nd respondent.
The document being relevant for adjudication of the case on hand, is taken on record by allowing the application.
It is to be noticed that objection is not filed to the said application.

5. Sri. Nagaraj C.Kolloori, the learned counsel for the respondent-insurer would submit that though the respondent-insurer has insured the vehicle, the vehicle being a goods vehicle, the insurer has insured only the driver and the cleaner.
The person, who has filed the claim petition seeking compensation is neither the driver nor the cleaner whereas he was an unauthorized gratuitous passenger in the vehicle.
Since the insured has not taken the policy covering the risk of gratuitous passenger, the insurer cannot be made liable to pay compensation.
It is further stated that the driver, in his cross-examination, has admitted that he did not possess necessary driving licence to drive the vehicle in question.

6. The learned counsel for the 4th respondent would submit that the 4th respondent purchased the vehicle on 26.11.2007, whereas the accident in question has taken place on 19.10.2007 prior to the purchase of the vehicle.
Thus, there cannot be any liability on him.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant has also relied upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Naveen Kumar Vs. Vijay Kumar and Others reported in (2018)3 SCC 1 wherein it is stated that the liability to pay compensation in respect of the injuries or death suffered on account of the motor vehicle accident is on the registered owner of the vehicle as on the date of the accident.

entities.text: Naveen Kumar Vs. Vijay Kumar and Others reported in (2018)3 SCC 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. From the contentions raised at the Bar and also from the records, it is forthcoming that the accident in question took placed on 19.07.2010 and as on that date, the vehicle stood in the name of the 2nd respondent- financier.
This being the position, the 4th respondent is not liable to pay compensation as the vehicle was transferred in his name on 26.11.2007.
9. As far as the contention of the insurer is concerned, it is to be noticed that the insurer has successfully established that the driver did not possess necessary driving licence.

10. The learned counsel for the insurer would rely upon the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Balu Krishna Chavan Vs. The Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Others (SLP (C)
No.33638/2017) and would urge that unless the liability of the insurance company is established,
there cannot be an order for pay and recovery.

sentences.text: Sri .N.C.Kolloori, learned counsel for the insurer would contend that the policy issued by the insurer would cover the risk of one person i.e. the driver of the vehicle.
Though the vehicle was built to carry one more person other than the driver, risk of the passenger is not covered by paying additional premium as required.
Admittedly, the vehicle is a goods vehicle.
Under Section 147(1)(b)(i) of the MV Act, the liability of the insurer extends to the person who is the owner of the goods carried in the vehicle or the authorized representative.
He would submit that it is not established by the claimant that he was traveling in the goods vehicle as the owner of the goods or as the authorized representative of the owner of the goods.

12. To this, learned counsel for the claimant would submit that the claimant was traveling in the vehicle as owner of the goods and this fact is established from the recital in the complaint, where one more passenger who was traveling in the vehicle has clearly stated that the claimant is the person who was traveling along with goods (iron rods).

13. Sri.N.C.Kolloori would submit that mere recital in the complaint is not sufficient to hold that the claimant was the owner of the goods and further submits that the very reading of panchanama carried out by the investigating police, it is apparent that the goods in the vehicle is not established.
He would further submit that no other documents are produced to show that the iron rods were found in the vehicle which was involved in the accident and the same was carried in the vehicle.
14. This Court has considered the contentions raised at the bar in this regard.
The complaint is filed by a coolie on the date of accident itself.

In the complaint the complainant has stated that his employer Shivappa Ramachandra Panchaput is working as a mason and on the date of accident the complainant and six other persons were traveling in the autorickshaw and his immediate employer has placed iron rods belonging to him in the autorickshaw.

15. It is to be noticed that the statement is not made by the claimant and is made by the complainant who is one among the co-passengers and claim petition is filed by one person who has sustained injuries in the accident.
Remaining six persons have not filed any claim petition.
It is nobody's case that iron rods which are said to be carried in the autorickshaw is belonging to some other person other than the claimant or his employer.

Merely because the police have not disclosed existence of iron rods in the autorickshaw while drawing the panchanama, it cannot be said that the iron rods were not carried in the vehicle when the vehicle was involved in the accident.
The panchanama would clearly reveal that autorickshaw had toppled at the place of accident and it is quite natural that immediately after the accident, there will not be panchanama by the police.

By the time panchanama was complete there would be few changes in the scene of accident and it is quite possible that iron rods might have fallen from the vehicle and it might have been removed from the vehicle immediately after the accident.
- 10 - The complaint is filed by the coolie who was traveling in the vehicle and it is extremely difficult to hold that recital relating to the iron rods were introduced to claim compensation.

Considering the fact that the complaint is lodged on the very same day, this Court is of the view that existence of iron Shivappa Ramchandra Panchaput @ ... vs Yashwant Siddappa Narasannawar on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149588934/
4 rods (goods) in the vehicle is established by the claimant.

sentences.text: That being the position, this Court has to take a view that the claimant is the person who was traveling in the goods vehicle along with goods and risk of the claimant is covered.

16. It is to be noticed that Sri.N.C.Kollori learned counsel for the insurer would contend that the defence that the driver of the vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident, is duly established.

Since this Court has taken a view that respondent No.2 was the owner of the vehicle as on the date of accident on the basis of additional document produced before the Court, the insurer is entitled to recover the compensation from respondent No.2.
- 11 - 17.

Since this Court has taken a view that respondent No.2 is owner of the vehicle at the time of accident, there cannot be any liability on respondent No.4.
18.
Since the claim petition is also filed seeking enhancement, this Court has to consider whether there are any grounds to enhance the compensation as claimed by the appellant.
19. The records would reveal that the claimant has sustained amputation of his arm.
The doctor has assessed disability at 65%.
The Tribunal has assessed functional disability at 50%.
The Tribunal has taken Rs.3,000/- p.m. as the income of the claimant.

Since the accident is of the year 2007, by referring to the chart prepared by High Court Legal Services Committee, Dharwad, this Court is of the view that Rs.4,000/- p.m. is to be taken as income of the claimant.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 20. Considering the fact that the claimant is a coolie, this Court is of the view that loss of income has to be assessed by taking functional disability at 60%.

Since - 12 - there is 60% disability and he was aged 45 years at the time of accident, 25% is to be added towards future prospects by following the ratio laid down in ERUDHAYA PRIYA Vs. STATE EXPRESS TRANSPORT CORPORATION LIMITED reported in AIR 2020 SC 4284.

entities.text: ERUDHAYA PRIYA Vs. STATE EXPRESS TRANSPORT CORPORATION LIMITED reported in AIR 2020 SC 4284
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, compensation payable towards loss of future income would be:
Rs.4,000 income + 25% future prospects x 12 months x 14 multiplier x 60% disability = Rs.5,04,000/-
21.

As far as compensation under the head of medical expenses at Rs.20,000/- is concerned, learned counsel for the appellant is not in a position to show that the claimant is entitled to higher compensation under the said head.
22. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.60,000/- towards pain and suffering.
Since this Court has assessed disability at 60%, it is appropriate to award Rs.80,000/- under the said head.

sentences.text: Since this Court has taken into consideration loss of future income by taking into consideration 60% functional disability and has also added 25% towards future prospects, this court is of the view that there is no need to award compensation under the head of loss of earning during laid up period and the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the said head same is set aside.
24. As far as conveyance, attendant charges is concerned, the same has to be enhanced by another Rs.10,000/-.
In all, the claimant is entitled to Rs.25,000/- under the said head.
25. As already noticed, the claimant has suffered amputation of left arm.
Because of amputation of left arm, the petitioner undoubtedly is deprived of various pleasures and amenities in life and compensation of Rs.30,000/- under the said head by the Tribunal is inadequate.
The same is enhanced by another Rs.1,20,000/-.
In all, Rs.1,50,000/- is awarded under the said head.
In all, the claimant is entitled to Rs.7,79,000/-.

The compensation shall carry interest at 6% p.a.
and the same shall deposited before the Tribunal within six weeks from today.
27. Appeal is allowed in part and the judgment and award of the Tribunal are modified as indicated above.

28. The insurer is entitled to recover the compensation from respondent No.2.
